title: Agentic RAG: Retrieve, Tools, Escalate
objective: After this lesson you will be able to route queries across retrieve/tools/direct/escalate paths, bound multi-hop retrieval loops, fuse tool results with retrieved context, and know when agentic machinery is overkill.
why: Static RAG pipelines answer one way; real traffic varies: order lookups need tools, greetings need direct answers, hard cases need humans, complex questions need iterated retrieval. Agentic RAG routes per need and loops with budgets — the LangGraph/CrewAI patterns applied to retrieval. Used where variability demands, never as default decoration.

blocks.text: Four paths, one router: **direct** (greetings, FAQs from memory — no retrieval), **retrieve** (policy/catalog knowledge), **tools** (live records: orders, inventory, prices), **escalate** (attacks, out-of-scope, low-confidence money). Route on need signals (order IDs → tools, SKUs → retrieve+filter, chitchat → direct, injection → quarantine) with confidence fallback to safe defaults.

blocks.caption: Signals route; uncertainty escalates; default stays safe

blocks.text: 'Compatible accessories under $50' needs hops: product → specs → compatible list → prices. **Bounded iteration**: each hop retrieves with the accumulated context, a done-check asks 'answerable now?', max-hops caps (3–5), visited-set prevents cycles. Same termination discipline as agent loops (LangGraph Ch.5/CrewAI Ch.5) — retrieval edition.

blocks.caption: Hops accumulate with cycle guards; budgets convert hangs to escalations

blocks.text: Order tools return live records; retrieval returns policy/catalog knowledge — generation needs both, labeled by source ('your order shows X; policy allows Y'). Fuse with source tags intact: tool facts (fresh, authoritative for records) outrank retrieved text on conflicts, and conflicts themselves surface to the answer ('records differ from policy text — escalated') rather than resolving silently.

blocks.title: Route the traffic
blocks.note: Run it: expect 5/5 with zero MISS. Each path exists for a need class; the default (retrieve) stays safe and cited. Routing tests enumerate like LangGraph Ch.4 — same discipline, retrieval flavor.

items: Route by need (direct/retrieve/tools/escalate/quarantine) with safe defaults and confidence fallback
Multi-hop with budgets, done-checks, visited-sets — termination by construction
Fuse tool records + retrieved knowledge with source tags; conflicts escalate, never silently resolve

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice router and confirm 5/5. (b) Add a sixth case of your design that breaks routing (ambiguous need) and state the fallback it should hit. (c) Sketch the visited-set scenario: which two-hop cycle does it prevent, concretely?
hints: Baseline 5/5; each path exercised once including quarantine.
Ambiguous example: 'My order (no ID) is wrong' — no order pattern, no clear policy need → retrieve default with low-confidence escalation rule.
Cycle: accessories → product → accessories (mutual references) — seen-set stops re-fetching; without it hops ping-pong to budget.
exercise.why: Fallback design (ambiguous → safe default) plus cycle analysis (concrete ping-pong killed by visited-sets) are the two robustness judgments agentic RAG lives or dies on.
exercise.code: // Robustness pattern: default-safe routing + visited-sets + budgets.

quiz.q: 'Where is order 4821?' through static RAG pipeline. Problem?
options: Live record needs the order tool — static retrieval answers from stale chunks; route by need (tools for records)
quiz.explain: Records vs knowledge: tools serve live state, retrieval serves documented knowledge. Need-routing sends each to its source.

quiz.q: Multi-hop loop without visited-set or budget. Risk?
options: Ping-pong cycles + unbounded hops — termination needs seen-sets, done-checks, and caps
quiz.explain: Iterative retrieval inherits loop hazards: mutual references cycle, vague goals never complete. Bound all three or hang on traffic.

quiz.q: Tool says shipped, policy text says 2-day late apology owed. Answer?
options: Fuse with source tags and surface the tension (records vs policy) — conflicts escalate visibly, never resolve silently
quiz.explain: Source-tagged fusion preserves provenance; silent resolution fabricates agreement. Conflicts are escalation material with both cited.

summary: Need-routed paths, budgeted multi-hop loops, source-tagged fusion with visible conflicts. Agentic where variability demands; pipelines where fixed.
